summary: The parent-keyed dependent fan-out (performance, workout_details -- no bulk list endpoint, one HTTP request per already-synced workout) is now bounded and resumable per sync invocation, via a new planDependentSync (internal/cli/sync.go) that every dependent sync call goes through instead of unconditionally enumerating the entire local store. Three composable rules, applied in order: (1) resumability -- by default, workouts that already have a dependentResource record are skipped (presence in provider_payloads IS the durable 'done' signal, correct regardless of id ordering or new arrivals, no separate cursor needed), while --full ignores existing records and instead resumes across repeated --full calls via a persisted offset (sync_state, keyed distinctly as `<resource>:full_progress` so it can't collide with the existing per-invocation --full cursor-reset loop), wrapping back to a fresh pass once a full pass completes; (2) run-scoping -- a new dependentScopeSincefor(...)/db.ParentIDsTouchedSince(...) restricts a dependent's candidates to only the workouts THIS invocation's flat phase actually touched when --latest-only is in effect and 'workouts' was flat-synced this run, so 'refresh the top' stays bounded end to end instead of silently fanning out over the whole store; (3) --max-parents (new flag) caps how many dependent fetches happen per invocation, emitting a sync_warning(reason=max_parents_cap_hit) event when it truncates the pending set, without failing the run. syncPerformanceDependent/syncWorkoutDetailsDependent were refactored to accept a pre-resolved dependentSyncPlan instead of computing ids internally, and their near-identical fetch/store loops were factored into one shared runDependentFanOut engine parameterized by resource name and a buildRequest closure -- fixing the pre-existing code duplication between the two as a byproduct. New store primitives: Store.ExistingProviderFactIDs(family) and Store.ParentIDsTouchedSince(family, since). Any future regen must keep both dependent functions routed through planDependentSync/runDependentFanOut with this same bounding contract; a fresh dependent added later (a third parent-keyed resource) should follow the same pattern rather than reintroducing an unbounded full-store fan-out.
reason: NEW ISSUES B and C from a second live post-fix verification sweep, confirmed as genuinely coupled: (C, the blocking one) a large account's dependent fan-out is ~2 requests x every synced workout with no bulk endpoint for either -- for a ~3.5k-workout account that's ~7000 sequential-ish calls, far exceeding any MCP client tool-call timeout, and critically it meant BLOCKING #1's every_n=1 fix (this session, performance-sync-every-n-default.json) could not actually be applied to an already-synced large store through the MCP surface at all, since the sync needed to realize it couldn't complete within one call. (B) separately, --latest-only is documented as 'refresh the top... caps pages at 1' but the observed behavior fanned a dependent phase out over the ENTIRE local store regardless, so a call that looked bounded by --latest-only silently wasn't. Presented three design options to the user (resumable cap+resume scoped by run / background+pollable-status / just-document-the-limitation); user chose the recommended cap+resume design with an explicit --latest-only scoping example, which this patch implements faithfully.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. New unit tests directly exercise planDependentSync (skip-existing default, --full ignoring existing records, --full resumability across repeated calls with wraparound after a complete pass, --dry-run not persisting progress, --max-parents capping both modes, scopeSince restricting to touched-since parents) and dependentScopeSinceFor's RunE-level wiring decision (4 case matrix). Live-verified against the user's real account end-to-end: (1) a plain sync --resources workouts cascade into performance/workout_details still works unchanged for a small batch; (2) sync --resources performance --full --max-parents 2 run three times in a row against 6 real records correctly processed 2, then 2, then 2, with sync_warning(max_parents_cap_hit) on the first two calls and a clean completion on the third; (3) after syncing 2 additional new real workouts, a plain (non-full) sync --resources performance correctly reported {"total":0,"reason":"already_up_to_date"} with success=1 (not a false warning) since the earlier cascade had already picked up the 2 new ones via default skip-existing behavior.
